script.title: The story of the first helicopter to fly on Mars
script.description: Discover how NASA's Ingenuity helicopter achieved historic powered flight on Mars. Explore its record-breaking mission and engineering feats.

shots.narration: This is the first aircraft to fly on another planet, hovering above Mars.
Here the helicopter operates in air about one percent as dense as Earth's sea‑level atmosphere.
To generate lift, its carbon‑composite rotors spin at roughly 2,400 revolutions per minute.
It weighs 1.8 kg and its two rotors span 1.2 metres, demanding precise engineering.
On 19 April 2021 it hovered three metres for about 39 seconds, the first powered flight on another world.
Originally planned for five test flights in 30 days, the mission continued far beyond that schedule.
Over almost three years it completed 72 flights, traveling more than 17 km across the terrain.
It climbed to 24 metres and reached 36 km/h before a rotor blade was damaged in January 2024.
Inside the craft is a small piece of fabric from the Wright brothers' 1903 Flyer.
